items.title: Pixel-UMI: Learning Environment-Aware Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensorized Human Demonstrations
items.summary: Pixel-UMI learns whole-body robot policies from sensorized human demos by retargeting trajectories using scene geometry and head/gripper data.
items.whyItMatters: It enables robots to adapt human skills to varied environments, improving deployment flexibility.

items.title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
items.summary: Pixel is a co-designed full-stack robot system integrating hardware, data collection, control, and learning for general-purpose mobile manipulation.
items.whyItMatters: It streamlines development, reducing mismatches and accelerating advanced robot capabilities.

items.title: From Natural Language to Exact Cover: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach to Zebra Puzzles
items.summary: The paper presents a neuro-symbolic method converting natural language into exact cover for solving zebra puzzles, addressing LLMs' logical reasoning gaps.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it enhances reliable reasoning in AI systems.

items.title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
items.summary: WebHarbor offers 153 realistic, executable web environments for training and evaluating GUI agents, addressing instability and limited coverage of live sites.
items.whyItMatters: It enables more reliable, authentic agent development by providing stable, diverse, and authenticated web scenarios.

items.title: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap
items.summary: The paper examines whether Muon’s pretraining speed advantage over AdamW persists during fine-tuning, finding that with enough pretraining data AdamW can close the gap.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it informs optimizer choice for efficient large‑model training and deployment.

items.title: Not All Reasoning Generalizes: A Case Study on Learning Generalizable Reasoning Strategies in RLVR
items.summary: The paper explores how reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards can teach large language models generalizable reasoning strategies, using an equation‑solving framework.
items.whyItMatters: It shows a path to more robust, transferable LLM reasoning, valuable for advanced AI applications.

items.title: FADE: Factored Ability--Difficulty Filtering for Online RLVR Scheduling
items.summary: FADE proposes a factored filtering method for online RLVR scheduling, selecting only prompts with mixed outcomes to efficiently improve policies.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it reduces wasted computation and accelerates learning in reinforcement learning systems.

items.title: Thought-deciphering via hierarchical EEG-to-text alignment
items.summary: The article discusses a new hierarchical EEG-to-text alignment method for brain‑computer interfaces that could help people with severe communication disabilities.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a non‑invasive way to restore speech for patients with locked‑in syndrome or similar conditions.

items.title: D&A: Decoupling Description and Assessment Enables VLMs as Zero-Shot Robotic Reward Models
items.summary: The paper shows how separating description from assessment lets VLMs estimate robot task progress without bias, improving zero-shot reward modeling.
items.whyItMatters: It offers more accurate, unbiased progress feedback for autonomous robots, boosting learning efficiency.

items.title: Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents
items.summary: The article introduces Strategist, a meta-agent that automates evolving inference strategies for AI agents across tasks.
items.whyItMatters: It promises reusable, adaptive reasoning, reducing manual coding for AI developers.

items.title: Tracing the Scientific Discovery Capacity of LLMs to Their Training Data
items.summary: The article investigates how an LLM’s ability to discover scientific facts can be traced back to the distribution of facts in its training data.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding this link helps improve model reliability and guide data curation for scientific AI.

items.title: Benchmark Prediction with Sparse and Unpaired Cached Responses
items.summary: The paper proposes a Product Kernel method to predict benchmark scores from sparse, unpaired model responses, reducing evaluation cost.
items.whyItMatters: It enables faster, more efficient model benchmarking for tech researchers and practitioners.

items.title: Efficient Closure Learning in Dynamical Systems: A Comparison of Data-Assimilated and Embedded Approaches
items.summary: Increased computing power has transformed computational science and improved predictive capabilities for complex systems, but many phenomena still exceed current simulation capabilities or require rapid evaluations for fast design iterations. Closure models address this challenge by approximating unresolved effects in reduced or incomplete dynamical systems. Data-driven closures offer a flexible…

items.title: ufakzeka-kulak: Building and Evaluating a 31.6M-Parameter Turkish Speech Recognizer from Scratch
items.summary: ufakzeka-kulak is an open Turkish speech-to-text model of 31.6M parameters, a FastConformer encoder with a token-and-duration transducer (TDT) and a CTC head, trained from scratch and released under Apache-2.0. It writes cased, punctuated Turkish with numbers as words. Its 4,977 training hours come from sources whose licences allow commercial use; 281 hours are human-transcribed, and for the…

items.title: DiabAgent: Toward Agentic Physiological Control
items.summary: As pretraining scales, medical language models have advanced rapidly in clinical question answering. Their ability to achieve effective physiological control through sustained intervention still lacks systematic quantitative evaluation. Type 1 diabetes provides a concrete setting: impaired insulin secretion creates dependence on exogenous insulin, with dosing continually adjusted using…

items.title: Four Bridges: Measuring Deception Propensity in a Multi-Agent Game
items.summary: AI agents are increasingly deployed in settings where they interact and coordinate with other agents, yet honesty is mostly measured in single-turn, single-agent benchmarks that pressure the model to deceive. We study deception that emerges in multi-agent interaction without any instruction to deceive. We introduce Kradle, a platform for evaluating AI models, and Four Bridges, an information…

items.title: Should We Combine Our Data? Algorithms and Limits for Privately Assessing Data Sharing
items.summary: In this paper, we study when two parties should pool their data to train a machine learning model. Two agents, Alice and Bob, each hold a sensitive labeled dataset and want to train a classifier from a given hypothesis class H. Even when each party's dataset can be perfectly classified on its own, the two parties may follow conflicting labeling standards or have selection biases that affect their…

items.title: Structured Visual Landscape: Generating Preferred Representations in Biological and Artificial Neural Networks
items.summary: Understanding how neurons respond to visual stimulus is an important question in both deep learning and neuroscience. It has significant implications for enhancing the interpretability of black-box artificial neural networks and for understanding the visual representation in the human brain. We propose a structured visual representations landscape and design an activation-based prior that allows…

items.title: Spacetime Emergence in the Memory of a Learning Agent
items.summary: We show that the causal structure of spacetime can emerge within the memory of a learning agent performing a quantum information task. We train a model-based reinforcement-learning agent to maximize the quantum mutual information between localized quantum probes interacting with a quantum field in Minkowski spacetime, without directly providing it with information regarding the spacetime metric…

items.title: DynaSolver: A Neural Operator for Autoregressive 4D Flow Prediction with Dynamic Boundaries
items.summary: Neural operators provide efficient surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD), but most are designed for static geometries and are not equipped to model unsteady flows induced by continuously moving boundaries.
